title: The Borrowed Inventory
premise: Wren Marchetti, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste five years ago, has survived by writing exquisite evasions — praise calibrated to say nothing. When the Marchetti family house is scheduled for auction, Wren returns to a home where their father, Judge Aldous Marchetti, once ran informal 'hearings' that settled neighbors' disputes outside any court, and where Wren's testimony as a child destroyed a family friend. As siblings Halcyon and Devvie maneuver to control the sale, Wren discovers the auction is being orchestrated by the son of the man their father ruined, who wants not the house but an admission. The novel ends with Wren testifying again — this time voluntarily, at a final hearing held in the empty dining room — trading the family's silence for the truth, losing the house but recovering, faintly and imperfectly, the taste of salt.
about_author: Sebastian Yarrow is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing menu copy before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town he refuses to name, and claims he can still remember what his grandmother's kitchen smelled like, which he considers his greatest literary asset.

chapters.title: The Palate of Others
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At an awards dinner, Wren delivers a rapturous review speech for a meal they cannot taste, hiding behind borrowed language from old notebooks. A young chef asks what the dish actually tasted like, and Wren lies beautifully. Emotional beat: the loneliness of fluent performance.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The certified letter arrives: the Marchetti house enters auction in six weeks. Wren reads the legal language aloud, tasting nothing, remembering everything. Flashback fragments surface unbidden — the dining room table, the gavel-shaped letter opener. Emotional beat: dread disguised as paperwork.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Halcyon's POV. The eldest sibling runs numbers on the estate, treating memory as depreciation. She wants a fast sale and no ceremony; she has spent her life converting feeling into assets. She calls Wren 'the sentimental one' with contempt and envy braided together. Emotional beat: grief managed as logistics.

chapters.title: Devvie Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Devvie's POV. The youngest sibling arrives before anyone expected, already living in the house, sleeping in the childhood bedrooms on rotation. Devvie claims it's caretaking; it looks like occupation. They've been corresponding with someone about the auction. Emotional beat: love expressed as territorial claim.

chapters.title: The Hearing Room
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks the house alone and finds the dining room exactly as Father kept it: the long table, the seating chart pinned inside the sideboard, neighbors' disputes archived in labeled boxes. The system of extralegal justice Aldous ran for thirty years, laid out like evidence. Emotional beat: awe curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Paid
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs via the archive. Through case files, we learn how the hearings worked: favors, verdicts, quiet debts. One file — the Okafor case, 1998 — has pages missing, and Wren's childhood handwriting appears in the margin. Emotional beat: the past asserting itself through paper.

chapters.title: A Man Named Okafor
chapters.summary: New character POV: Elias Okafor Jr., the buyer quietly engineering the auction through intermediaries. His father was ruined by a Marchetti verdict and died indebted. Elias doesn't want the house; he wants the family assembled in it, one last time, under rules they'll recognize. Emotional beat: patience sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Dinner Without Verdicts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. First shared meal in the house in years. Halcyon proposes selling contents separately for maximum return; Devvie sabotages by playing recordings of Father's old hearings. Wren realizes both siblings are negotiating around the same avoided question. Emotional beat: familial tenderness weaponized.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reconstructs the Okafor file from memory: at eleven years old, Wren testified that Mr. Okafor struck his own son — testimony Father elevated to verdict, though Wren now suspects the child was coached. The taste loss began within a year. Emotional beat: horror arriving slowly, like cold water rising.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren attempts to write a review and produces pure evasion, then burns the draft in the kitchen sink. A phone call to their editor admits, obliquely, that something is broken. The chapter interleaves restaurant memories with the Okafor kitchen Wren once described in testimony. Emotional beat: confession rehearsed, aborted.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Debt
chapters.summary: Halcyon's POV. We learn Halcyon secretly owes money and needs the auction's timeline desperately — and that she knew about the missing pages years ago and chose silence to protect Father's legacy, which protected her inheritance. Emotional beat: complicity dressed up as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Devvie's Recordings
chapters.summary: Devvie's POV. Devvie has been cataloguing every hearing recording since Father's death, believing the archive is the real inheritance. They reveal they've been speaking with Elias for months — not betrayal, they insist, but curation. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as its own kind of ambition.

chapters.title: The Appraiser
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under the guise of a pre-auction appraisal, Elias walks the house with Wren. He never accuses; he only asks questions shaped like furniture. In the dining room he says, 'Your father settled things here. I'd like something settled.' Emotional beat: menace conducted with perfect courtesy.

chapters.title: Salt Test
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Alone, Wren conducts an experiment: tastes salt, sugar, lemon. Nothing. Then, eating cold rice from the childhood kitchen out of a chipped bowl, a ghost of flavor — gone instantly. Hope becomes more painful than absence. Emotional beat: grief briefly inverted.

chapters.title: The Sibling Vote
chapters.summary: All three siblings. A formal vote on the auction terms collapses when Wren demands the Okafor file be read aloud before anything is sold. Halcyon threatens lawyers; Devvie sides with Wren, shocking everyone. The family fractures along the exact lines Father designed decades ago. Emotional beat: open war.

chapters.title: Father's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the sideboard, Wren finds Aldous's private journal: he doubted the verdict, documented his doubt, and ruled anyway because the hearings required certainty to function. Power, he wrote, cannot afford hesitation. Emotional beat: understanding without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Terms of Settlement
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias makes his offer explicit: withdraw the engineered buyer pressure, let the house sell fairly — if the Marchettis hold one final hearing, on the record, with Wren testifying to what really happened in 1998. No money changes hands. Only words. Emotional beat: justice proposed outside the law, mirroring the original sin.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The night before, Wren practices testimony in the empty dining room, addressing chairs. Halcyon appears in the doorway and, instead of arguing, tells the story of the day of the verdict from her own thirteen-year-old eyes — the first time either sibling has spoken of it. Emotional beat: reluctant solidarity.

chapters.title: The Final Hearing
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The hearing itself: Devvie keeps the record, Halcyon reads the file, Elias sits where his father sat. Wren testifies — not to a clean truth, but to the coaching, the doubt, the child's hunger to be believed. The verdict of 1998 is formally vacated by the only court that ever issued it. Emotional beat: catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Rotating sibling POVs. The house sells at auction, publicly and fairly, to a young couple who see only light and square footage. Halcyon signs with steady hands; Devvie donates the hearing archive to the county historical society; Wren watches strangers walk through the dining room without knowing what happened there. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: What Wren Tasted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, at an ordinary diner, Wren eats eggs and toast and tastes them — faintly, uncertainly, possibly imagined. The review Wren writes afterward is short, plain, and true. The editor calls it the best thing they've published. Emotional beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing. Wren visits the archive at the historical society and adds a final document: their own testimony, filed beside their father's verdicts, completing the record. Walking out past the auction sign's remains, Wren buys salt at a corner store just to keep some in their pocket. Emotional beat: carrying the past forward, lightly.
